findings.title: Incorrect field info extraction overrides field name
findings.explanation: The overridden _extract_field_info replaces the original field name with the environment variable name for both positions, which can break mapping of settings fields to their values. This may cause settings to be populated with wrong keys or miss values.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the original field name when constructing the tuple, e.g., `return list((x[0], field_name, x[2]) for x in super()._extract_field_info(field, field_name))`.
findings.verdict_reason: The change makes _extract_field_info return tuples where the field name is replaced by the environment variable name, matching the finding’s claim, but without reviewing the base implementation we cannot confirm this breaks functionality or is mitigated elsewhere.

findings.title: Ambiguous tuple construction in _extract_field_info
findings.explanation: The comprehension uses `x[0]` twice to construct a tuple `(x[0], x[0], x[2])`. This duplication is confusing and makes it hard to understand what the tuple elements represent. It also obscures the intent of the returned data structure, potentially leading to maintenance errors.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the tuple elements with meaningful names or use a namedtuple/class to clarify the structure, e.g. `return [(name, name, is_sensitive) for name, _, is_sensitive in super()._extract_field_info(field, field_name)]`
